description: A person who loves machine, learning some Machine Learning
summary:
Long-duration deep-space missions expose astronauts to communication delays of 20+ minutes each way, making real-time consultation with flight surgeons impossible. Drawing on
NASA's Human Research Program framework of spaceflight hazards, we built an offline-first health monitoring dashboard that detects autonomic stress from heart rate variability
(HRV) data — before symptoms appear.
Astronauts upload a standard RR-interval CSV exported from any HRV-capable wearable. The system extracts time-domain and frequency-domain HRV features (mean HR, RMSSD, SDNN, LF/HF ratio), runs a lightweight RandomForest classifier trained on the WESAD stress dataset, and displays a color-coded triage report with plain-language recovery guidance.
The entire inference pipeline runs CPU-only with no network connection, on hardware as lightweight as a Raspberry Pi 5 (model: 666 KB, inference: 11ms/window, peak RAM: 237 KB), making it deployable as an isolated spacecraft medical workstation.
details:
▎ What it does and how it works

▎ Astronaut Health Monitor is an offline-first HRV (Heart Rate Variability) stress detection dashboard for long-duration space missions. The astronaut exports a standard

▎ RR-interval CSV from any HRV-capable wearable and uploads it to the dashboard. The system extracts time-domain and frequency-domain HRV features (mean HR, RMSSD, SDNN, LF/HF

▎ ratio) over 2-minute sliding windows, runs a RandomForest binary classifier, and displays a color-coded triage report (NOMINAL / STRESSED) with plain-language recovery guidance

▎ (paced breathing, hydration, rest).

▎

▎ Benefits and intended impact

▎ Deep-space missions introduce communication delays of up to 24 minutes each way, making real-time consultation with flight surgeons impossible. This system gives crews an

▎ autonomous, onboard tool to detect autonomic stress before acute symptoms appear — enabling early self-care and reducing mission health risk. The inference engine runs CPU-only

▎ with no network connection (model: 666 KB, inference: 11 ms/window, peak RAM: 237 KB), making it deployable on hardware as lightweight as a Raspberry Pi 5 acting as an isolated

▎ medical workstation.

▎

▎ Tools and technologies

▎ Python · NumPy · SciPy · scikit-learn (RandomForest) · Streamlit · pandas · joblib. Training dataset: WESAD (Schmidt et al., ICMI 2018), a peer-reviewed wearable stress

▎ benchmark used as a spaceflight analog. Hardware target: Raspberry Pi 5 (ARM64 Linux).

▎

▎ Creativity and design decisions

▎ Rather than requiring proprietary sensors or cloud infrastructure, the system is wearable-agnostic — any device that exports RR intervals works, covering a wide range of

▎ commercial and mission hardware. The offline-first architecture was a deliberate constraint: every design decision (model size, inference speed, RAM footprint) was evaluated

▎ against the question "can this run on a Pi 5 with no internet?" The dashboard is designed for non-physician users — plain language, color-coded status, and one clear action per

▎ triage result.
dataRefs: NASA Human Research Program — 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
